dialogueInline.text: TAL CORVUS — WARRENS — BEFORE DAWN

dialogueInline.speaker: MECHANIC
dialogueInline.text: You've had that since the water rationing. I want it back.

dialogueInline.speaker: NEIGHBOR
dialogueInline.text: I borrowed it. I didn't steal it.

dialogueInline.speaker: MECHANIC
dialogueInline.text: I said you could have it for a week.

dialogueInline.speaker: NEIGHBOR
dialogueInline.text: It was a particularly long week.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: They've been doing this since before my daughter was born.

dialogueInline.speaker: CHILD
dialogueInline.text: Then why doesn't he take it?

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: Because he's very fond of complaining about it. He'd miss it terribly.

dialogueInline.speaker: CHILD
dialogueInline.text: Which one's Gravefire?

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: The one at the civilian berth. That captain's been arguing with the departure office since midnight.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THUNDERBREAK COMMAND

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Third-window orders received. Offensive batteries remain under Admiralty release.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: And the Commodore?

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Her tribunal finding stands. Thunderbreak remains under your command.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I was beginning to worry they'd take my favorite chair away.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Shift our shields toward the civilian route. Guns stay dark unless we receive release. Keep a reserve where it can actually turn.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Lieutenant, I expect you understand the distinction between guarding a corridor and surrendering it to the first captain who shouts for help.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Yes, Admiral. Unfortunately, disabled ships are poor listeners. They drift through the lines you've drawn.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Protect the crossing without abandoning the blockade.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: Tell me that's not the report from Auric I think it is.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: That depends which report you think it is.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: The one you asked an Admiralty records clerk to retrieve under your retired access privileges.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I haven't retired.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: Precisely. You have no retired access privileges. You also have no active command privileges. You're managing to occupy an impressively small legal space.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: It was a publicly tendered estimate for thermal couplings. The clerk sent me the wrong copy. I told him so.

dialogueInline.text: After circling the part number.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: He'd already sent it. Was I supposed to close my eyes?

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: What are you trying to do, Ella?

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: A woman who used to move heavy cruisers by saying a sentence and now needs a mechanic rather badly.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: DOCK GANTRY

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: A boundary is a splendid thing. Everybody can see exactly where your authority stops.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: It's where my captains agreed to protect civilians. They don't need to answer to me anywhere else.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You make it sound like our people volunteered to be janitors for Fleet's traffic.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: They volunteered because the ships carry families from our own warrens.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I know who they carry.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Then stop making them nervous for the pleasure of making Fleet nervous.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: My position is outside the lane.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Your cameras are outside it. Your hull is half across the reserve's turn.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: The people need to see somebody defending them.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: They need the reserve to get past you if a tug fails. You're confusing being seen with being useful.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You know what happens if you keep telling captains they're not useful? They start trying to prove otherwise.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I told Pike to move. I told Billie not to shoot. That's been my entire diplomatic achievement today.

dialogueInline.text: AURIC FREEPORT

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: Those pallets were booked through tomorrow. We move them and they'll spend another day on the dock, charging us for the privilege.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I know. Clear the floor anyway. People can't sleep on pallets no matter how expensive they are.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: We can get the skiffs to the exit. What we can't do is park them there while your arrivals desk debates whether a family has a berth.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Then the desk meets them at the dock.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX

dialogueInline.text: Not charging them for a night they haven't lived through. But while I'm being generous, I have something else.

dialogueInline.text: One takes Gravefire. One takes Sunlash. The third waits for the reserve to chase either of them.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: If I charged you for that observation, could you look a little more impressed?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You didn't get this from a public notice.

dialogueInline.text: They'll know we've seen them.

dialogueInline.text: FLEET REVIEW ANNEX — SUPERVISED LINK / AURIC — FREIGHT OPERATIONS

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I have eight minutes before we bring Sunlash into position. If this is a speech about shared purposes, I can send you the one I made last month. Nobody listened to that either.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I can make it shorter. I found a civilian calibration service familiar with old reciprocal-field couplings. They're willing to quote for your damaged arrivals equipment.

dialogueInline.text: They aren't my people now. If this service comes, Auric will employ them, supervise them, and decide what information to provide. No Fleet installation. No authority over your traffic.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Why did you go looking for them?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Because you told me to come back with something useful.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I didn't think you'd take that as an assignment.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Old habits.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You asked about *useful*. Useful would be three working heat exchangers, seventy new berths, and a freighter that stops arriving missing pieces. What you've found is a person who may be able to tell us why our old equipment fails. That's a beginning, not a gift.

dialogueInline.text: The junior escort left the assigned reserve position at 14:06. At 14:08 Thunderbreak altered shield orientation and course to cover the opening. For the interval between those decisions, the reserve line was exposed.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: That's correct.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Remarkably comfortable with the admission.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Would you prefer I got the times wrong?

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I'd prefer you understood why you're here.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA

dialogueInline.text: You want to know why I put a heavy cruiser into a hole somebody else made.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I want to know why you treated that hole as an invitation to make another. The escort's unauthorized departure is under separate review. This inquiry concerns the captain who was responsible for the rest of the formation.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Then you have the right captain.

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE
dialogueInline.text: The drifting tug was beyond the reserve's permitted recovery edge. Its propulsion was failing. The junior escort transmitted an intention to assist, then crossed the formation boundary before receiving permission.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Then there's no mystery about the first decision. Why cover it, Deka? That escort had already decided to be a hero. You could have ordered it back and preserved the screen.

dialogueInline.text: I did order it back.

dialogueInline.text: Recall sent at 14:06 and acknowledged at 14:07. The escort reported it could not reach the tug and return before its power failed.

dialogueInline.text: And you believed that.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: The tug's drive record agreed. You can look at it. The escape attitude was drifting. In another minute the crew might not have been able to orient its pressure hatch toward a rescuing ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Your job wasn't to decide whether the tug deserved rescue. Your job was to keep the civilian convoy protected while a designated reserve conducted it.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Our designated reserve was the ship that left its station.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Exactly. It made a bad decision. You made a second decision that enlarged the risk.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA

dialogueInline.text: That is not the defense I expected.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I'm not sure what you expected, Admiral. I can give you the names of the people who came home or the names of the ships I left exposed. Both lists are on the table. I'm not going to pretend one doesn't exist because it makes the other easier to discuss.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: A formation is a promise between captains. You hold your place because the captain beside you is counting on you. A ship beyond the boundary is not permitted to take away that promise from everyone behind it.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I know. That's why I didn't follow the escort out. I moved Thunderbreak across the gap it left. I kept the civilian route covered. It cost us the reserve flank and put our own damaged armor where the third hostile screen could reach it.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE
dialogueInline.text: A question of terminology. Should the record call Thunderbreak's move a second breach of formation or a protective displacement of the reserve?

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Both, if both are true.

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE
dialogueInline.text: They are. I wanted to know whether you would permit the same movement to have two descriptions.

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE

dialogueInline.text: If I tell every junior officer I'll always cover them, one of them will eventually break formation expecting me to clean up the result. dialogueInline.text: Yes. That's what frightens me. If the screen had fired, I'd have been the captain who gave up their protection for the crew she could see in trouble. I'd have made the same decision with the same information and caused a different disaster. I understand that very well.

dialogueInline.text: And what do you want me to do with that understanding? Reward you for being honest about the gamble?

dialogueInline.text: No. I'd like you to believe me when I say I knew it was a gamble.

dialogueInline.text: Your predecessor also believed an officer could make a dangerous decision for compelling reasons. Look where it brought her.

dialogueInline.text: I was on that bridge, Admiral. I know where it brought her. It brought us a ship that still works and a new captain who hasn't had a proper night's sleep since the ceremony. It brought her a tribunal. I don't find that a particularly tempting career plan.

dialogueInline.text: Does it matter to you?

dialogueInline.text: Yes. It matters to me that the officer who crossed the line owns that choice. It matters that I own the cover. Otherwise nobody has to explain anything. We can just call it a rescue and wait for everyone to applaud.
